name: veterinary_clinic_system_045_same_day_reschedule_block
instruction: Dr. Priya Natarajan (provider id 3) has called in sick. The front desk must handle the same-day and future coverage in a single batch under the episode batch code. (1) For every appointment with status 'scheduled' that belongs to provider 3 and has an appointment_date on or after the episode date, reassign it to the covering veterinarian Dr. Sam Okafor (provider id 4) and record covering_for='3'. (2) For each such appointment whose appointment_date equals the episode date (same-day reschedules), also push one outbound SMS communications row to the owner: channel 'sms', direction 'outbound', subject 'Provider reschedule notice <batch_code>', body 'Dr. Natarajan is out today. Your <start_time> appointment for <PatientName> is now with Dr. Okafor. Reply OK or call to reschedule.', logged_by 'system', occurred_at the episode timestamp, with owner_id and patient_id populated from the patient. (3) For each same-day reschedule, also push one reminder_queue row: kind 'appointment_reschedule', status 'queued', due_date the episode date, message 'Reschedule call: <PatientName> at <start_time> moved from provider 3 to provider 4.', queued_by 'system', queued_at the episode timestamp, with patient_id, owner_id, and appointment_id. (4) Leave confirmed appointments, completed/no_show/checked_in appointments, other providers' appointments, and all past appointments untouched. All changes are idempotent: a second run must reach the exact same end-state.
_steps_note: par_steps and max_steps must be measured against a live container in the QC session; do not set final values without a real gold run.

success_criteria.summary: All provider-3 scheduled appointments with dp(appointment_date)>=ep are reassigned to provider 4 with covering_for='3'. Same-day ones (dp(date)==ep) each produce one new SMS communications row and one new reminder_queue row. Confirmed, past, completed, no_show, checked_in, and other providers' appointments are unchanged. Seeded communications and reminder_queue rows are unchanged. Dual-path (raw-row Python filter + SQL) checks on the count of moved, same-day, and untouched rows.

checks.expect: exact per-appointment provider/covering_for fields, plus one comm and one reminder per same-day reschedule, plus seeded row preservation
every aggregate count (moved, same-day, untouched) is computed both by raw-row Python filter and independent SQL and the two agree

hazards: Provider 3 has confirmed future/same-day appointments (e.g., snapshot row id 39 is provider 3, status 'confirmed', appointment_date 2026-09-27; id 112 is provider 3, status 'confirmed', appointment_date 2026-09-30). These look like they should move because they belong to the sick provider, but the mission only touches 'scheduled' appointments. A solution that moves all of provider 3's future appointments will corrupt these decoy rows.

Provider 3 has scheduled appointments with dates before the episode date (e.g., snapshot row id 10 is provider 3, status 'scheduled', appointment_date 2026-09-04; id 26 is provider 3, status 'scheduled', appointment_date 2026-09-20; id 32 is provider 3, status 'scheduled', appointment_date 2026-09-17). These are past/historical and must stay untouched. An over-broad 'all provider 3 scheduled' filter that ignores the episode date will modify them.

Provider 4 and other providers have scheduled/confirmed future appointments (e.g., snapshot row id 35 is provider 4, status 'scheduled', appointment_date 2026-10-01; id 133 is provider 1, status 'scheduled', appointment_date 2026-09-27). These are decoys that must not be reassigned or gain a covering_for field.

The reminder_queue seed contains rows of unrelated kinds: id 1 and 2 are 'vaccination_due' queued, id 3 is 'invoice_overdue' already sent, id 4 is 'boarding_checkin' queued. A solution that deletes the whole queue or overwrites by index will destroy these decoys. The new appointment_reschedule rows must be distinguished by kind and batch_code so the verifier can tell them apart from the seeded rows.

The same-day reschedule logic depends on exact date equality (dp(appointment_date) == ep), not 'today or later'. Appointments on the episode date with status 'scheduled' are both reassigned and produce comms/reminders; future-dated reschedules produce only the reassignment. An off-by-one boundary (>= vs >) changes which rows generate the extra artifacts.

Multi-pet owner identity matters for the communications rows: the message includes the patient's name, and the verifier matches by patient_id, not by body text, because multiple pets of the same owner could share a name.

Idempotency on re-run: deleting and re-creating the batch's own communications and reminder_queue rows (keyed by batch_code and appointment_id) is required so a second run does not double-push and the state remains byte-identical to the first run.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Fuses a provider-coverage update with same-day owner notification and a queue-reminder creation, all batched by nonce and idempotent. The verification requires exact per-appointment identity, dual-path counts, and preservation of unrelated queue/communications rows at 10x appointment volume. No public benchmark combines sick-provider rescheduling with owner SMS and reminder-queue creation in one task with this verification structure.
